title: Field with its own contract: seen factor, second-order terms, fall and clock

key_results.statement: Class: every member of $\mathcal D$ and every nondegenerate eigenvector $\varphi_0$ of $C_f$, $\varepsilon=0$ or $\varepsilon>0$; regime: none (R0); status: exact. $\hat C=\hat C_b\otimes\mathbb 1_c+\sum_xP_x\otimes\kappa xX$ with $\hat C_b=A+\sum_xP_x\otimes[N(x)\sigma_3\otimes(m+D)+e_0]$, the member of $\mathcal C$ with $\zeta_x=1$, $m_x=mN(x)$, $\eta_x=N(x)$, $V_x=e_0$; $\hat C$ is the contract of an admissible description of $b$ and $c$.

Class $\mathcal D$, R0, exact: under (2.20) $N(x)\to N(x)+a_x$, $e_0\to e_0+c$, while $\varphi_0$, $\tilde\Phi_x$, $S$, $\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f$, $\nu$ and $\hat C$ are unchanged; $N(x)$ is well defined only together with the coefficient of $B_x$ in $C_{br}$ (zero in the form of $\mathcal D$).
Class $\mathcal D$, every start of the body, no condition on $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$; status: bound, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda$.

Class $\mathcal D$; regime R1: $2\epsilon_1+2\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3<1$ with $\epsilon_3=\nu M_{\max}/\Delta_f$, weak records; status: order estimate of the constant, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le2\epsilon_1[1+O(\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)]$.

Class $\mathcal D$, every schedule of readings on $b$ and $c$: bound $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert\le2\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda_k$ for all $\lambda_k\ge0$ without conditions; in R1 (order estimate, fixed schedule) $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert=O(\epsilon_1^2)+O(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f\lambda_k)$, so the statistics are those of a sharp field with profile $N(x)$ through first order in $\epsilon_1$ on $\lambda\ll1/(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f)$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1: $H_{\rm eff}=\hat C-\tfrac12(\mathcal S_1^{\dagger}W_1+W_1^{\dagger}\mathcal S_1)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$ with $\mathcal S_1$ the solution of the Sylvester equation; for the exact $H_{\rm eff}$, $\lVert\Pi_0\Psi(\lambda)-(e^{-iH_{\rm eff}\lambda}(\phi\otimes\chi))\otimes\varphi_0\rVert\le2\epsilon_1^2[1+\dots]$ for all $\lambda\ge0$ (order estimate of the constant); a truncation $H'$ adds at most $\lambda\lVert H_{\rm eff}-H'\rVert$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact coefficient of the second order in $\epsilon_1$ at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: $H^{(2)}=-\sum_x\gamma_xP_x\otimes\mathbb 1_2\otimes(m+D)^2\otimes\mathbb 1_c$ with $\gamma_x=\langle\varphi_0\vert\tilde\Phi_xS\tilde\Phi_x\vert\varphi_0\rangle$, $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert\le\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_f$, $\lVert H^{(2)}\rVert\le\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact first corrections with an order estimate of the remainder $O(\epsilon_1^2(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2\Delta_f)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$: $H^{(2,1)}=-\tfrac\tau2\sum_x(c_xh_x\otimes(-i\sigma_1)+c_x^{*}h_x^{\dagger}\otimes(i\sigma_1))\otimes\mathcal M^2$ with $c_x=\tfrac12(\rho_{xx}+\rho_{x+1,x+1})+\rho_{x+1,x}$, and $H^{(3)}=\sum_x\gamma^{(3)}_xP_x\otimes\sigma_3\otimes\mathcal M^3$; $\lVert H^{(2,1)}\rVert\le2\tau\epsilon_1^2$, $\lVert H^{(3)}\rVert\le\epsilon_1^2\epsilon_3\Delta_f$; $\hat C+H^{(2)}$ reproduces the statistics to accuracy $\eta\gg\epsilon_1^2$ for $\lambda\lesssim\eta/[\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3+\epsilon_1^2)]$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with first corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: on the level $k$ the on-site block is $(N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3)\sigma_3+(e_0-\gamma_xM_k^2)\mathbb 1_2$ and the hopping block is $-\tfrac{i\tau}2(1-M_k^2c_x)\sigma_1$; the body part is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ except for the hopping phase (present iff $\operatorname{Im}\rho_{x+1,x}\neq0$), and of $\mathcal C$ at leading order iff $\gamma_x=0$ for all $x$; all new terms are well defined under (2.20).

Class: linear profiles $\Phi_x=N_0+xY$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$, leading order in $\kappa$; status: closed forms: $\tau_k=\tau(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)$, $\hat M_k=M_k(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)$, $G_k=gM_k+\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^3$, $\mathcal F_k=\gamma_1M_k^2$, $g_{\zeta,k}=-4M_k^2\operatorname{Re}\rho_Y$, $V_k=e_0-\gamma_0M_k^2$; a level offset is a common phase for a start in one level.

Class: linear profiles of the field, branch starts at rest; regime R1 as in (10.12); status: closed form with remainder $O(\varepsilon^4)$ and second corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]$ with $\beta=g(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)-\gamma^{(3)}_1$, $\lvert\gamma_1\rvert M_k\le2\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_YM_{\max}/\Delta_f$, $\rho_0M_k^2\le\epsilon_1^2$.

Class and regime of (10.13), exact at the stated order: at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and every $N\ge2$, level-independence of $a_{k,+}(0)$, of $a_{k,-}(0)$ and of both with one value $-\tau^2g$ each hold iff $\gamma_1=0$; with the first corrections, for $N\ge3$ iff $\gamma_1=0$ and $\beta=0$, for $N=2$ upper iff $\gamma_1+\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, lower iff $\gamma_1-\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, both iff $\gamma_1=\beta=0$; the independence is lost at order $\epsilon_1^2$, leading order in $\epsilon_2$.

Class: linear profiles; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with first correction in $\epsilon_3$; status: closed form: $E^+_{x,k+1}-E^+_{x,k}=\frac{2\pi}{N\lambda_0}[N(x)-\gamma_x(M_k+M_{k+1})+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_k^2+M_kM_{k+1}+M_{k+1}^2)]$; at leading order independent of $k$ iff $\gamma_x=0$ or $N=2$.

Class: linear profiles, starts $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$; regime R1 at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and at the orders of (3.36); status: order estimate: the clock statistics is the ring-clock mixture (3.36) with every advance shifted by $-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma\lambda/\lambda_0$ (rate $\bar r(x_0)$ in the wide-start limit) up to total variation $\le\tfrac12\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2\lambda$, so to accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2)$ if $N\ge3$, and for all $\lambda$ if $N=2$ or $\gamma_{x_0}=0$.

Class: linear profiles; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$; status: closed form of the leading defect: with $\bar r(x)=[N(x)-\gamma_x\Sigma]/\lambda_0$, $\mathcal R_k=a_{k,+}(0)+\tau^2(\bar r(x+1)-\bar r(x))/\bar r(x)=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma]$, $\Sigma=M_0+M_{N-1}$; the relation (4.24) holds for all levels iff $\gamma_1=0$ and $g\gamma_0=0$.

Class: independent cells, every $\Delta_x>0$, $n_x>0$, $\varepsilon_x\ge0$; regime R1 with $\epsilon_3=\epsilon_1$; status: exact evaluation of the coefficients: $N(x)=n_x$, $\varepsilon=\max_x\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f=\min_x\Delta_x$, $\gamma_x=\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$, $\rho_{xy}=\delta_{xy}\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2$, $c_x=\tfrac12(\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2+\varepsilon_{x+1}^2/\Delta_{x+1}^2)$, $\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$; the body part of $H_{\rm eff}$ is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$.

Class: one cell with the body at $x$, branch sign $\pm$, level $k$; status: exact: the cell contract $C_{f_x}\pm M_k\Phi_x$ has the lower eigenvalue $\pm M_kn_x-\Omega_{x,k}$ and the upper eigenvalue $\pm M_kn_x+\Omega_{x,k}$ with $\Omega_{x,k}=\sqrt{\Delta_x^2/4+M_k^2\varepsilon_x^2}$; overlap of the lower eigenvector with the cell start $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)=[\tfrac12(1+\Delta_x/2\Omega_{x,k})]^{1/2}$; at leading order in $\tau/\Delta_x$ the hopping block is multiplied by $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)\cos(\alpha_{x+1,k}/2)$.

Class: cells with $n_x=1+gx$, branch starts at rest; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first order in the gradients of the cell data; status: closed form: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+2g\rho_0M_k^2]$; control $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$ constant: the branch-odd term vanishes, while the level offsets, the defect $\tau^2g\gamma\Sigma$ of (4.24) and the level-dependent hopping remain.

Class $\mathcal D$ (linear profiles for fall, clock and relation), regime R1, status: order estimate: the factor seen, the level-independence of the fall from rest, the one-rate ring clock and the relation (4.24) are unchanged at order $\epsilon_1$ and first change at order $\epsilon_1^2$ at the leading order of the coefficient in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, with relative size $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert M_{\max}\le\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f/M_{\max}$.

open_issues: The two small numbers of the question do not control the class D: a third one, ε3 = ν·M_max/Δ_f, enters the conditions and the first corrections; whether it becomes part of the regime of the question is for the main model.
(10.6), the R1 part of (10.7) and the remainders of (10.10) are order estimates: their constants and the dependence of (10.7) on the number of readings are not bounded explicitly.

The accelerations (10.13) and (10.20) are those of the description with H_eff; for the description with C only the agreement of the statistics within (10.10) is derived, not a statement about its acceleration.

(10.16) has the orders of (3.36), zeroth order in the gradients; the loss of clock coherence by the level-dependent force, which separates the levels in position at first order in the gradients, is not treated.
Where 2ε1 + 2ε2 + ε3 ≥ 1 (a slow field) the expansion fails and only (10.1), (10.2), (10.4) and the first part of (10.7) remain.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: γ_x is an inverse cost, γ_x·M_k² a cost, ρ·M_k², γ1·M_k and β·M_k² pure numbers like g, accelerations τ² times a number as in (4.16).
Sharp field ε = 0: all new coefficients vanish, H_eff equals the compression, the excited component is zero and (2.3) is recovered; field operators commuting with C_f force ε = 0.
Cell: the exact lower eigenvalue and overlap reproduce the second-order on-site term, the vanishing third-order term and the hopping factor obtained from the general formulas.
